newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, short-dated swaps down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, short-dated swaps down.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah returned to its opening level against the dollar late on Friday after a short-lived weakening in the morning, dealers said.
They said short-dated swap rates fell on relative scarcity of overnight dollar supply in the interbank market.
One Japanese bank dealer said focus was mainly on the swap market following a narrowing of interest rate differentials.
But longer-term swap rates were stable.
He said overnight deposit rates for the U.S. currency edged up to 6.0/6.25 percent from the usual of 5.5 percent as demand suddenly increased in the past few days.
The Japanese bank dealer said operators were seen buying today dollars and selling value tomorrow and/or spot rupiah which dragged short-dated swap rates down.
"The money market was well supplied to finance the dollar purchases for now. This seemed to have enabled some short-term speculation following shifting of interest rates," he said.
"Jakarta-based offshore banks were also seen taking up dollars from the market," he said.
Dealers said dollar supply in the money market was rather thin at present which caused the uptrend and reduced interest rate differentials between the two currencies.
